title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Ava Chen
body:
Purpose
---
This document codifies Redwood Inference's standard processes and manager responsibilities for hiring, onboarding, performance and feedback cycles. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new managers to ensure consistent candidate experience, fast ramp, and fair performance evaluation across the company.

Scope
---
Applies to all full-time employees, contractors (hired >6 months), and hiring managers at Redwood. Supplemental role-specific rules (e.g., exec hiring, security-sensitive roles, or customer-facing enterprise roles) are in related pages.

Owner and Review Cadence
---
- Primary owner: People Ops (hiring & onboarding processes)
- Secondary owners: Recruiting, Hiring Managers, HRBP
- Review cadence: annual (People Ops leads last review date in metadata) or on major policy change.

1) Hiring: Requisition to Offer (high level)
---
Goal: Deliver a predictable, equitable, and timely hiring process with clear handoffs. Target SLA: 45 days from req approval to offer acceptance for non-executive roles; time-to-fill measured per requisition.

Steps (numbered procedure)
1. Create requisition
   - Hiring manager completes Job Requisition Form (internal link) with role profile, headcount justification, expected level, proposed salary band, and interview panel recommendations.
   - Owner: Hiring manager. People Ops must approve budget and band within 2 business days.
2. Sourcing & screening
   - Recruiting posts role to approved channels and runs active outreach.
   - Initial screen (30 min) performed by recruiter to verify fit and salary expectations.
   - Owner: Recruiter. SLA: initial screens within 7 days of posting.
3. Interview loop design
   - Typical loop (Engineering): Recruiter screen -> Hiring manager phone -> 3 technical interviews (system design, team-fit, coding/arch) -> final manager interview -> bar raiser and/or cross-functional partner as needed.
   - Typical loop (Product/Sales): Recruiter screen -> Hiring manager -> product design exercise -> cross-functional partner interview -> leadership interview.
   - Interviewers must use standard scorecard and sample questions (see Scorecards section).
4. Candidate evaluation and debrief
   - Debrief within 48 hours of final interview. Collect written scorecards from every interviewer. Hiring manager synthesizes and posts decision with consensus.
5. Offer approval and compensation
   - Offer packet prepared by recruiter. Compensation must align to published bands and go through Offer Approval Matrix:
     - Base within band: Hiring manager + Recruiter sign-off.
     - Base above band or individual contributor >L5: Hiring manager + People Ops + VP approval.
     - Executive roles: Chief People Officer + CEO approval.
   - Target: Offer sent within 3 business days after decision.
6. Reference and background checks
   - People Ops runs reference and required background checks in parallel with offer acceptance.
7. Acceptance & onboarding kickoff
   - Once candidate accepts, trigger new-hire workflow and pre-boarding tasks.

Candidate experience rules
- Interviewers must acknowledge interview invites within 24 hours.
- Feedback must be documented in the central ATS (scorecards) within 48 hours.
- Communication: Recruiter owns candidate updates at least weekly until decision.

Scorecards and interviewing standards
---
Every interview now uses the canonical scorecard fields (explicit questions and rating scales). Minimum required fields:
- Core competencies for role (technical depth, system design, product sense, collaboration)
- Example evidence (what the candidate said/did)
- Recommendation: Strong Hire / Hire / Weak Hire / No Hire
- Bias mitigation checkbox (was a structured question used?)

Behavioral interviewing reminders
- Use STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) prompts.
- Avoid illegal or protected-class questions. See HR compliance quickguide.

Interview training
- All interviewers must complete Interviewer Training (required annually). New managers must shadow at least two interviews before owning their first loop.

2) Offer & Compensation: Approval matrix (summary)
---
- IC levels L1-L3: Hiring manager + Recruiter approval.
- L4-L5: Hiring manager + People Ops signoff.
- L6+ or managers: People Ops + VP approval.
- Any equity/RSU exceptions or signing bonuses require CPO approval.
- For remote hires in different geographies, compensation is determined by location banding; consult People Ops for local benefits.

3) Onboarding: Pre-boarding to 90 day ramp
---
Goal: Get new hires production-ready and socially integrated within first 90 days while minimizing administrative friction.

Pre-boarding (triggered at acceptance)
- Recruiter / People Ops actions (within 24 hours): send welcome email, collect forms, schedule Day 1 logistics, create IT ticket for laptop and account provisioning.
- Hiring manager actions: schedule first week calendar (Day 1, intro meetings, onboarding training), invite mentor/buddy, share 30-60-90 expectations.

Day 1 checklist
- HR & People Ops: new-hire orientation (benefits overview, policies, payroll), send access list and code of conduct.
- IT: deliver laptop or confirm provisioning; ensure accounts (G Suite, Slack, JIRA, internal infra) are ready.
- Manager: 1:1 welcome (30-60 min), team intro, review role, first-week goals.

Week 1 (orientation + context)
- Required trainings: security & compliance (within 72 hours), data privacy, and any role-specific compliance.
- Technical onboarding: run local dev setup guide and README exercise.
- Social: intro to cross-functional partners and assigned buddy.

30-60-90 day plan (manager + new hire)
- 30 days: Onboarding complete; contributor independently completes small deliverables; understands codebase and processes.
- 60 days: Delivers meaningful work, participates in team rituals, reliable contributor for scoped projects.
- 90 days: Fully integrated; measurable impact delivered and initial feedback conversation completed.

New hire checklist (compact table - pipe-delimited)
| Item | Owner | SLA |
|---|---:|---:|
| Offer letter signed & returned | Candidate / Recruiter | Before start date |
| Laptop & accounts provisioned | IT | Day 0 (before Day 1) |
| Security & compliance training completed | New hire | 72 hours |
| First 1:1 scheduled | Manager | Day 1 |
| Buddy assigned | Manager | Day 1 |

Role of the buddy
- Peer-level contact for cultural onboarding and immediate questions. Not a manager substitute. Recommended commitment: first 30 days, weekly check-ins.

4) Performance, feedback, and review cycles
---
Principles
- Frequent, timely feedback is preferred to heavy annual surprises.
- Reviews should be evidence-based, tied to goals and competencies, and calibrated across teams.

Cycle overview
- Continuous feedback: Ongoing – encourage real-time praise/feedback in Slack and 1:1s.
- Manager check-ins: Weekly 1:1s required for first 90 days; thereafter cadence is manager-led (recommended weekly or biweekly).
- Mid-year check-in: informal calibration (June/July) focused on progress against goals.
- Annual performance review: formal review (November cycle) including self-assessment, manager assessment, calibration, and compensation decisions.

Performance scoring and calibration
- Use our standard competencies (Execution, Technical/Role Mastery, Collaboration, Leadership where applicable).
- Scores: Exceeds / Meets / Below expectations. Expand with narrative examples.
- Calibration forum: people-ops facilitates cross-team calibration meetings to normalize expectations and prevent grade inflation.

Promotion & compensation cycles
- Promotion criteria: demonstrated mastery of next-level competencies, sustained impact, and manager + peer endorsements. Promotions typically synchronized with the annual review cycle or via promotion packet submission (ad-hoc promotions require manager + People Ops + VP sign-off).
- Compensation adjustments: determined in compensation window post-calibration. People Ops publishes the compensation calendar annually.

5) Feedback best practices for managers
---
- Deliver feedback often and in private for corrective conversations. Use specific examples and suggested actions.
- Balance strengths and growth opportunities. Start with impact and tie to company goals.
- Document significant feedback and development plans in the HR system to support review evidence.
- For performance concerns: begin with a documented performance plan (PIP for sustained Below Expectation over two consecutive review cycles). People Ops must be engaged before initiating formal performance improvement measures.

6) Manager responsibilities (hiring, onboarding, performance)
---
Hiring
- Build clear role profile and interview loop.
- Interview consistently and promptly (scorecards due within 48 hours).

Onboarding
- Own the first 90 days: schedule check-ins, set 30-60-90 goals, assign buddy, and ensure team integration.
- Ensure required trainings are completed and resources shared.

Performance
- Hold weekly 1:1s during ramp; document goals and feedback.
- Prepare evidence for calibration and compensation discussions.
- Support career conversations and promotion readiness.

Manager checklist (short)
- Approve requisition and interview loop
- Participate in interviewer training
- Create 30-60-90 plan before Day 1
- Run weekly 1:1s in the first 90 days
- Submit promotion or compensation proposals with evidence

7) Probation, exits and offboarding handoffs
---
- Standard probationality: first 90 days considered initial evaluation period for new hires. Managers should hold a 30-day check-in, a 60-day check-in, and a 90-day performance discussion.
- Early concerns: escalate to People Ops immediately; remediation steps documented.
- Offboarding: reference the offboarding policy (related page). People Ops coordinates final pay, benefits termination, and access revocation; manager ensures knowledge transfer.

8) Exceptions, edge cases, and escalation paths
---
- Executive hiring (C-level): follow Executive Hiring Playbook (separate page), requires Board/Founder-level approvals.
- Hiring for regulated or customer-sensitive roles: additional security screening and contract language required; consult Security & Compliance.
- Escalations: unresolved hiring disputes or offer exceptions escalate to Head of People Ops. Performance-related disputes escalate to HRBP + Head of People Ops.

Templates and artifacts (where to find them)
---
- Job Requisition Form, Scorecard templates, Offer letter templates, New hire checklist, 30-60-90 plan template: stored in People Ops templates folder (link).
- Interview training slides and anti-bias resources: People Ops learning page.

Appendix: Sample 30-day onboarding agenda (engineer)
---
Day 1: Orientation, accounts, team lunch, 1:1 with manager (expectations).
Day 2-5: Local dev setup, run first README task, meet key cross-functional partners, complete security training.
Week 2-4: Take ownership of small bugfix/feature, weekly check-ins with manager, end-of-30 day feedback meeting.

Document maintenance
---
- Owner: People Ops. Please request edits via the Confluence comment thread or send suggested changes to people-ops@redwood.ai. This document will be reviewed at least annually or when major process changes occur.

Frequently asked questions (short)
---
Q: Who approves exceptions to bands?
A: People Ops + VP; exec exceptions require CPO.

Q: How do I request a hiring freeze exception?
A: Submit a business case to People Ops and Finance; approvals required from Head of Product/Engineering and Finance.

Q: What if a new hire needs equipment before start?
A: Include urgent equipment request in the pre-boarding form; People Ops will prioritize IT provisioning.

End of document.
